chunks: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

I asked him about someone who said, “By Allah,” and then did not fulfill it. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Its expiation is feeding ten needy people, a mudd each of flour or wheat, or freeing a slave, or fasting three consecutive days if he cannot find anything.”

key_terms.إِطْعَامُ: feeding as a form of kaffarah
key_terms.مَسَاكِينِ: needy persons eligible to receive the food
key_terms.مُدًّا: a mudd measure given to each needy person

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for breaking an oath sworn by Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for expiation when a person swears by Allah and then does not fulfill the oath. It specifies the kaffarah as feeding ten needy people, or freeing a slave, or fasting three consecutive days when one cannot do the other forms.
